summary: Verified LinkedIn cookie fix. Backend: POST /api/li-search/cookie accepts only li_at (no JSESSIONID), returns {success:true, warning:...} even when Voyager /me validation fails, and saves the cookie. GET /api/li-search/cookie returns has_cookie=true after save. Search endpoint accepts requests with saved cookie. Frontend: cookie input form is always visible, button label reads 'Update' when a cookie exists, and the warning is displayed as a green success-styled message (not an error). All 4 backend tests passed; UI verified via Playwright.
critical_code_review_comments: The 'success' response returns a warning string that literally says 'cookie may be expired or invalid' — this can confuse end users. Consider softening: 'Cookie saved. Full validation could not be completed; try running a search to verify.'
linkedin_search.py is 1000+ lines — should be split into cookie/search/messaging modules per code review guideline (>700 lines).
bare 'except:' at line ~370 in save_cookie fallback should catch specific exceptions.
MongoDB _id is correctly excluded in most places but some responses (messages log, posts) stringify _id (acceptable, but ensure no ObjectId is returned raw).
Cookie is saved with `validation_warning` field but this field is never surfaced to the user via GET /cookie — consider returning it so the UI can display a persistent warning banner.
seed_data_creation: Test cookie 'AQEDAQxxxxxxxxfake_ui_test_cookie' saved in li_search_config collection via UI test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified for LinkedIn cookie validation. The endpoint gracefully saves cookies even when Voyager /me returns 302/403/401, returning success:true + warning. Frontend keeps the cookie form visible with 'Update' button label when cookie already saved. Since we cannot use a real LinkedIn cookie, actual search functionality against LinkedIn was not exercised end-to-end (search job is fired but backend calls to LinkedIn will fail with 401 — expected).
rca of the issue: N/A — this is a verification of an already-applied fix, all expected behaviors confirmed.
